zh.principle: **标准**：数字身份指南（Digital Identity Guidelines）。留存的这份文件是《数字身份指南》的 B 分册，不是合订的总纲：扉页在编号行之下给出分册题「Authentication and Authenticator Management」，免费获取地址行写「This publication is available free of charge from」行后印着 DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-63B-4，即本文件为 B 分册的第 4 版。摘要自述对象：「This guideline focuses on the authentication of subjects who interact with government information systems over networks to establish that a given claimant is a subscriber who has been previously authenticated.」并交代它定什么：「This document defines technical requirements for each of the three authentication assurance levels.」两处措辞与分册题一致：产出是按等级给出的技术要求，范围止于认证与 authenticator 管理。
zh.why: §1 先把认证拆开定义：「Authentication is the process of determining the validity of one or more authenticators used to claim a digital identity by establishing that a subject attempting to access a digital service is in control of the secrets used to authenticate.」要补的缺口是对手能力的差别，分级正是为此：「Stronger authentication (i.e., a higher AAL) requires malicious actors to have better capabilities and to expend greater resources to successfully subvert the authentication process.」两段合起来说明风险不在算法而在控制关系：要判定的是声明者是否掌握相应秘密，等级则按对手须付出的能力与资源分档。
zh.used: 义务是双向的。§2 对声明者提出要求：「To satisfy the requirements of a given AAL and be recognized as a subscriber, a claimant SHALL authenticate to an RP (or IdP, as described in [SP800-63C]) with a process whose strength is equal to or greater than the requirements at that level.」§3.1.1.2 把口令的具体约束落到验证者与 CSP：「Verifiers and CSPs SHALL require passwords that are used as a single-factor authentication mechanism to be a minimum of 15 characters in length.」以及「When processing a request to establish or change a password, verifiers SHALL compare the prospective secret against a blocklist that contains known commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords.」三条引文同时约束两端：声明者所用过程的强度不得低于该等级，验证者与 CSP 则对口令长度与黑名单比对负有 shall 级义务。
zh.broken: 限度写在四处。摘要划出目的边界：「The guidelines are not intended to constrain the development or use of standards outside of this purpose.」§1 划出场景边界：「It does not address the authentication of a person for physical access (e.g., to a building).」同节承认自愿泄露无从拦阻：「The protections at the various AALs are intended to protect against credential theft and are not intended to protect against willful disclosure of credential secrets by a subscriber.」§3.1.1 对最常见的凭证写得更直白：「Passwords are not phishing-resistant.」四条合起来是：目的之外的标准发展它不管，人员物理准入它不管，订阅者自愿共享或泄露没有技术手段可拦，而口令本身不抗钓鱼。
zh.history: 扉页写「NIST SP 800-63B-4 Digital Identity Guidelines Authentication and Authenticator Management」，即 B 册第四版；摘要末句直说：「This publication supersedes NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-63B.」出版史块给出被取代的那一版「Supersedes NIST SP 800-63B (June 2017; updated March 2, 2020)」与评审日期「Approved by the NIST Editorial Review Board on 2025-05-30.」；引用行给出七位作者与 2025 年：「Temoshok D, Fenton JL, Choong YY, Lefkovitz N, Regenscheid A, Galluzzo R, Richer JP (2025) Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Authenticator Management.」扉页日期为 2025 年 7 月，DOI 行给 DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-63B-4。目录行号所指的合订总纲与 A、C 两册不在这份文件里。四段引文合起来是这份文件的版本事实：分册号、被取代的上一版及其更新日期、评审批准日期、作者名单与年份。

en.principle: **Standard**: Digital Identity Guidelines (数字身份指南). The retained file is Part B of the guidelines rather than the umbrella document: below the number line the title block gives the part title "Authentication and Authenticator Management", and the free-access line reads "This publication is available free of charge from" line is followed by the DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-63B-4, which marks it as the fourth edition of Part B. The abstract states its subject: "This guideline focuses on the authentication of subjects who interact with government information systems over networks to establish that a given claimant is a subscriber who has been previously authenticated." and states what it defines: "This document defines technical requirements for each of the three authentication assurance levels." Both phrasings agree with the part title: the output is per-level technical requirements, and the range is authentication and authenticator management.
en.why: Section 1 first unpacks the term: "Authentication is the process of determining the validity of one or more authenticators used to claim a digital identity by establishing that a subject attempting to access a digital service is in control of the secrets used to authenticate." The gap being closed is the difference in attacker capability, which is what the levels encode: "Stronger authentication (i.e., a higher AAL) requires malicious actors to have better capabilities and to expend greater resources to successfully subvert the authentication process." Read together, the two sentences locate the risk in a relation rather than an algorithm: what has to be established is control over the secret, and the levels are graded by the capability and resources an attacker must expend.
en.used: The duties run in both directions. Section 2 addresses the claimant: "To satisfy the requirements of a given AAL and be recognized as a subscriber, a claimant SHALL authenticate to an RP (or IdP, as described in [SP800-63C]) with a process whose strength is equal to or greater than the requirements at that level." Section 3.1.1.2 puts the concrete password constraints on verifiers and CSPs: "Verifiers and CSPs SHALL require passwords that are used as a single-factor authentication mechanism to be a minimum of 15 characters in length." and "When processing a request to establish or change a password, verifiers SHALL compare the prospective secret against a blocklist that contains known commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords." The three quotations bind both ends at once: the claimant must use a process at least as strong as the level, while verifiers and CSPs carry shall-level duties on password length and on blocklist comparison.
en.broken: The limits are stated in four places. The abstract bounds the purpose: "The guidelines are not intended to constrain the development or use of standards outside of this purpose." Section 1 bounds the setting: "It does not address the authentication of a person for physical access (e.g., to a building)." The same section concedes that voluntary disclosure is out of reach: "The protections at the various AALs are intended to protect against credential theft and are not intended to protect against willful disclosure of credential secrets by a subscriber." And section 3.1.1 is blunt about the most common credential: "Passwords are not phishing-resistant." Read together: standards development outside this purpose is not constrained, physical access authentication is not handled, deliberate sharing or disclosure by a subscriber meets no technical countermeasure here, and passwords by themselves do not resist phishing.
en.history: The title block line reads "NIST SP 800-63B-4 Digital Identity Guidelines Authentication and Authenticator Management", i.e. the fourth edition of Part B, and the abstract records the supersession: "This publication supersedes NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-63B." The publication-history block names the edition it replaces, "Supersedes NIST SP 800-63B (June 2017; updated March 2, 2020)", and the review date, "Approved by the NIST Editorial Review Board on 2025-05-30." The citation line gives the seven authors and the year: "Temoshok D, Fenton JL, Choong YY, Lefkovitz N, Regenscheid A, Galluzzo R, Richer JP (2025) Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Authenticator Management." The title block is dated July 2025 with the DOI DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-63B-4. The umbrella Part 1 and Parts A and C are separate publications and are not in this file. The four quotations together are the edition facts of this file: the part number, the edition it replaces with its own update date, the approval date, and the author list with the year.

zh: AAL：认证保证等级，本文件为三级各定技术要求。
authenticator：证明声明者掌握相应秘密的凭证。
verifier：执行认证过程的角色，可由 CSP 或 IdP 承担。
CSP：凭证服务提供者，维护订阅者账户。
claimant：正在请求访问数字服务的主体。
phishing-resistant：能抵御钓鱼的认证方式，AAL2 起必须提供该选项。
en: AAL: authentication assurance level; this file sets technical requirements for each of three levels.
Authenticator: the credential that shows the claimant controls the corresponding secret.
Verifier: the role that performs the authentication, held by a CSP or an IdP.
CSP: credential service provider, the party that maintains the subscriber account.
Claimant: the subject attempting to access a digital service.
Phishing-resistant: an authentication method that withstands phishing, required as an option from AAL2 up.
